programme: PCGF2 (PRC1 Polycomb subunit, MEL18) represses HOXA7 while KMT2A (MLL1, Trithorax-group H3K4 methyltransferase) activates the same gene, HOXA7, the canonical Polycomb/Trithorax bistable switch at a HOX locus; KDM5C, an H3K4 demethylase, erases KMT2A's activating mark and shares three targets with KMT2A directly (FGFR1, ME3, RRP8), acting as the repressive counterweight to KMT2A at that shared gene set; HOXB6, a paralogous HOX-cluster gene regulated by this same writer/eraser/Polycomb machinery, is the phenotypic readout showing altered expression in both tissues.
role_in_a: In COPD-affected airway epithelium, this Polycomb/Trithorax balance at HOX loci is expected to set the differentiation/patterning state of airway epithelial cells during chronic injury and repair; HOXB6 itself is directly reported with altered expression in emphysema, a core COPD phenotype.
role_in_b: In esophageal cancer, the same writer/eraser/Polycomb machinery is documented acting on squamous epithelial identity: KMT2A carries genomic alterations in ESCC, KDM5C inhibition affects an esophageal cancer cell line, and midcluster HOXB genes (the HOXB6 family) are epigenetically silenced during progression from Barrett's-type precursor lesions to squamous neoplasia.
shared_axis: Both the COPD airway and the esophageal squamous epithelium are chronically injured stratified/pseudostratified epithelia whose regional identity is held in place by the Polycomb (PCGF2)/Trithorax (KMT2A) switch at HOX loci, fine-tuned by the H3K4 demethylase KDM5C; repeated smoke or reflux injury in either tissue could push this same chromatin switch toward a dedifferentiated, HOX-dysregulated state, giving emphysematous remodeling in lung and dysplastic/neoplastic transformation in esophagus a shared molecular substrate rather than a shared cause.
reasoning: The module is concretely nameable — PCGF2 and KMT2A converge on HOXA7, KMT2A and KDM5C converge on FGFR1/ME3/RRP8 — and three of the four carrying factors (HOXB6, KMT2A, KDM5C) are independently placed in the literature in at least one of the two diseases. But PCGF2 itself has no direct evidence in either disease, COPD is anchored by a single paper, and nothing retrieved states a direct COPD–esophageal-cancer link through this axis, so the cross-disease connection still rests on chromatin-biology reasoning rather than a documented shared finding; concordance across patient groups is also moderate (75–84 of 299, ~25–28%), not near-universal.
support: PMID 11238043 — reports HOXB6 among HOX genes with altered expression in human emphysema, placing it in COPD; PMID 22603795 — shows epigenetic regulation of midcluster HOXB genes (HOXB6's family) in esophageal precursor/neoplastic lesions, placing it in Esophageal_Cancer; PMID 33456985 — reports KMT2A genomic alterations in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma; PMID 33967558 — shows a KDM5C inhibitor affects the Eca-109 esophageal squamous cancer cell line, implicating KDM5C in esophageal cancer. No PMID above places PCGF2 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: Perform ChIP-seq for H3K4me3 (KMT2A mark) and H2AK119ub/H3K27me3 (PRC1/PCGF2 mark) at the HOXA7 and HOXB6 loci in matched COPD airway epithelial biopsies and esophageal dysplasia/ESCC biopsies; if the chromatin state at these loci is not concordantly shifted toward the same (activated vs repressed) direction in both diseased tissues relative to healthy controls, or if PCGF2/KMT2A knockdown in airway versus esophageal epithelial organoids fails to reciprocally move HOXA7/HOXB6 expression, the shared-module account is wrong.
caveats: This is a cross-tissue pairing (lung vs esophagus), so any shared programme must be a tissue-intrinsic epigenetic mechanism, not shared organ anatomy or an obvious clinical overlap; 299 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, limiting how independent the concordance signal really is. PCGF2 is included only on canonical Polycomb-biology grounds and its shared HOXA7 target with KMT2A in this network — it has zero direct literature or Open Targets association in either disease, so its role here is inferred, not retrieved. Tissue-generic exclusions already removed obvious lung/esophagus master regulators, so the absence of canonical epithelial identity factors (e.g., squamous master regulators) in this list is expected, not a gap. The single-view exclusions (TCF20, HDAC4, ZNF217, etc., each peaking near percentile 0.99 in one group but recurring in under 16% of groups) show that most apparent top hits do not generalize, underscoring that the surviving ~25–28% concordance for the carrying factors, while real, is a modest signal rather than a dominant one.
